text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- New Interior Minister Vidmantas Ziemelis thinks that the abolition of capital punishment in Lithuania is premature. Criminals should know they might be punished by the death sentence for especially violent crimes, the minister said on Monday after a series of crimes in northern Panevezhys.
- 36-year-old Lithuanian basketball star Rimas Kurtinaitis agreed to head the Sports Department of the country after his contract with the French Salon basketball club expires.
- Shares continued their rapid rise on the stock exchange.
- Lithuania extracted 151,000 tonnes of crude oil in 1996, 36,500 tonnes more than in 1995.
- Lithuania will negotiate the currency board model and import taxes with the IMF during a meeting scheduled for January 21 to February 4 when an IMF mission is in the country.
- The foreign loans of Lithuania rose by 1.144 billion litas in 1996 and was 4.679 billion litas at the beginning of the year. Foreign loans made up 15.8 percent of GDP.
- The transport ministry intends to suggest today to privatise up to 30 percent of Lithuanian Railways which has share capital of 1.2 billion litas.
- Parliament held a solemn meeting in parliament to commemorate the sixth anniversary of the January 13, 1991 hardline Soviet crackdown.

- Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas expects that Germany will understand better the aim of Lithuania to join the European Union and NATO after his recent visit to Germany, the minister says in an interview to the newspaper.
- A new licensing order might unexpectedly bloc the activity of four big international audit companies in Lithuania.
- Estonian investment company Talinvest acquired 87 percent of Lithuanian Suprema brokerage.
- Lietuvos Energija suffered 1.2 million litas of losses after repairing iced-up electricity lines.
- German packing company Pavel intends to invest in Lithuania this year. Representatives of the company visited four Lithuanian sewing factories.
